leftEvidence.title: Israel crosses the sea out of Egypt

compares.posture: Place the scenes side by side. Similar shape does not require identical meaning.

rightEvidence.title: Israel crosses the Jordan into the land

compares.tension: The first crossing moves Israel out; the second moves Israel in. The repeated form frames opposite directional transitions.
compares.title: Two crossings

leftEvidence.title: Dry land appears as waters are gathered

points.label: Result
points.right: A people escapes through the sea

compares.posture: Compare vocabulary and scene structure without claiming that one passage is simply a coded version of the other.

rightEvidence.title: Dry ground becomes Israel’s path through the sea

compares.tension: The language is close enough to invite attention and different enough to resist collapse.
compares.title: Dry ground appears twice

points.label: Body
points.left: A people walks on dry ground
points.right: A speaker imagines sinking without foothold

points.label: Question
points.right: How can the speaker be delivered?

compares.posture: Use the comparison to sharpen genre sensitivity rather than merge the passages.

rightEvidence.title: Deep water expresses a speaker’s peril

compares.tension: The same natural element can connect passages while performing completely different literary work.
compares.title: Water as scene / water as metaphor

leftEvidence.title: Water brings life wherever it flows

points.label: Source
points.left: Water flows from the temple area
points.right: River proceeds from the throne of God and the Lamb

points.label: Life
points.left: Living creatures thrive where it goes
points.right: The river is called water of life

points.label: Trees
points.right: Tree of life appears beside the river

points.label: Healing
points.right: Leaves are for healing of the nations

compares.posture: Track what is explicitly shared, then preserve what belongs uniquely to each vision.

rightEvidence.title: The river flows from God’s throne through the city

compares.tension: Revelation resembles Ezekiel strongly while reshaping the scene around its own final-city vision.
compares.title: Two rivers of life

concept.centerRule: Concept → character anchors → events, places, actions, tensions, and source passages. Characters carry the concept through the biblical narrative without making every occurrence mean the same thing.

characterAnchors.label: God
characterAnchors.note: Creates, separates, provides, judges, renews, and is repeatedly connected with the presence or gift of life-giving water.

characterAnchors.label: Noah
characterAnchors.note: The Flood places water around judgment, preservation, and a new beginning.

characterAnchors.label: Moses
characterAnchors.note: The sea crossing and wilderness water crises place water inside Israel’s deliverance and dependence.

characterAnchors.label: Israel
characterAnchors.note: The people cross water, thirst in the wilderness, and repeatedly encounter water as boundary, provision, and memory.

characterAnchors.label: Joshua
characterAnchors.note: Israel crosses the Jordan under Joshua as another generation enters a new stage.

characterAnchors.label: Naaman
characterAnchors.note: The Jordan becomes the setting for commanded washing and cleansing.

characterAnchors.label: John the Baptist
characterAnchors.note: The Jordan becomes the setting for baptism and preparation.

characterAnchors.label: Jesus
characterAnchors.note: Jesus enters the Jordan, speaks of living water, and becomes a central character wherever later water imagery gathers around life and renewal.

concept.throughline: Water moves through Scripture beside creation, judgment, survival, crossing, provision, cleansing, distress, renewal, baptism, conversation, and new creation. The recurring element stays recognizable while the characters, events, genres, and literary work around it change.

context.body: This is the opening creation sequence, before any human action or later water event.
context.label: Creation setting

observations.body: Darkness is over the deep while God’s Spirit hovers over the waters.
observations.label: Starting condition

observations.body: God separates waters and then gathers the waters below so dry land appears.
observations.label: Separation

observations.body: Dry land is named Earth, and the gathered waters are named Seas.
observations.label: Named places

observations.body: Water is present before the ordered spaces of sea and land are named.
observations.label: Sequence

dissects.posture: Notice the order of waters, speech, separation, gathering, and dry land before assigning a symbol.
dissects.tension: The passage shows waters being ordered, but it does not explain their origin or reduce them to one later meaning.
dissects.title: Waters gathered, dry land appears

compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

context.body: The scene follows entry into the ark and precedes the waters beginning to recede.
context.label: Flood sequence

observations.body: The waters increase until the ark rises above the earth.
observations.label: Rising

observations.body: The waters cover the high mountains under the whole sky.
observations.label: No remaining height

observations.body: The ark is carried while life on the dry land dies.
observations.label: Two outcomes

observations.body: The account closes by stating that the waters prevailed for 150 days.
observations.label: Prevailing waters

dissects.posture: Track what the rising water does to the ark, the land, the mountains, and living creatures.
dissects.tension: Water carries the ark and destroys life outside it; the passage preserves both effects without treating them as the same outcome.
dissects.title: Waters cover the earth

context.body: Israel has left Egypt but has not yet escaped Pharaoh’s military reach.
context.label: Departure from Egypt

observations.body: Israel reaches the sea while Egypt approaches from behind.
observations.label: Blocked route

observations.body: An east wind drives the sea back through the night and the waters divide.
observations.label: Wind and division

observations.body: The middle of the sea becomes dry ground for Israel.
observations.label: Dry path

observations.body: The water remains present as a wall on Israel’s right and left.
observations.label: Water on both sides

dissects.posture: Read the sea as part of the scene’s changing geography: obstacle, divided water, dry path, and wall.
dissects.tension: The element that blocks escape becomes the place of escape without ceasing to be the sea.
dissects.title: A path through the sea

compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

context.body: The delivered people now depend on provision in a place without water.
context.label: Wilderness travel

observations.body: The people camp at Rephidim and have no water to drink.
observations.label: No water

observations.body: The dispute about water becomes a question about whether the LORD is among them.
observations.label: Quarrel and test

observations.body: Moses passes before the people with elders as witnesses and strikes the rock.
observations.label: Before the elders

observations.body: Massah and Meribah preserve the testing and quarrel after water is supplied.
observations.label: Named memory

dissects.posture: Keep physical thirst, public quarrel, testing, command, witnesses, and provision in their narrated order.
dissects.tension: The water crisis is answered, but the place name keeps the people’s testing question open in memory.
dissects.title: Water from the rock

context.body: The crossing ends wilderness travel and begins Israel’s entry into the land.
context.label: Entry into the land

observations.body: The Jordan is overflowing its banks when the priests reach it.
observations.label: Flood stage

observations.body: The water flowing from upstream stands in one heap.
observations.label: Waters stopped

observations.body: The priests stand on dry ground in the Jordan while the people cross.
observations.label: Priests in the middle

observations.body: The action continues until the whole nation has crossed.
observations.label: Complete crossing

dissects.posture: Watch the river’s condition, the priests’ position, the stopped water, and the nation’s movement.
dissects.tension: The river is both a flooded boundary and the place where the priests stand until the crossing is complete.
dissects.title: The Jordan stops

compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

context.body: Naaman arrives with status and gifts but must receive an instruction he considers too small.
context.label: A foreign commander

observations.body: Elisha sends a messenger telling Naaman to wash in the Jordan seven times.
observations.label: A simple command

observations.body: Naaman expected Elisha to appear, call on God, and perform a visible act.
observations.label: Expected spectacle

observations.body: Naaman’s servants turn him back toward the command he first rejected.
observations.label: Servants persuade

observations.body: He goes down, dips seven times, and his flesh returns clean.
observations.label: Descent and return

dissects.posture: Follow command, anger, persuasion, descent into the river, repeated washing, and bodily change.
dissects.tension: The water is ordinary Jordan water, while the commanded act and its result challenge Naaman’s expectations about how cleansing should happen.
dissects.title: Naaman washes in the Jordan

context.body: This is poetic speech to God, not a narrated crossing or washing.
context.label: Prayer in distress

observations.body: The prayer begins with water reaching a point of bodily danger.
observations.label: Water at the neck

observations.body: Mire and depth remove any stable place to stand.
observations.label: No foothold

observations.body: Floods pass over the speaker rather than opening a route.
observations.label: Overflowing

observations.body: Deep water, a dry throat, and failing eyes combine into one account of distress.
observations.label: Body under strain

dissects.posture: Read the water as poetry: notice which physical features carry the speaker’s distress.
dissects.tension: The imagery connects this prayer with dangerous-water scenes while its literary work remains different from a report of physical travel.
dissects.title: Deep water as distress

context.body: The river belongs to Ezekiel’s vision of a restored temple and land.
context.label: Temple vision

observations.body: The water flows from the temple area toward the eastern region.
observations.label: Temple source

observations.body: The river moves away from the sanctuary and down toward the Arabah and sea.
observations.label: Outward flow

observations.body: The sea water changes where the river enters it.
observations.label: Water healed

observations.body: Living creatures and fish multiply wherever the river comes.
observations.label: Life follows

dissects.posture: Track the river’s source, direction, effect on the sea, and result for living creatures.
dissects.tension: The river’s source is fixed at the temple, yet its life-giving effect expands as it travels outward.
dissects.title: A river brings life

compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

context.body: The Jordan scene follows John’s preaching and precedes Jesus’ wilderness testing.
context.label: Beginning of ministry

observations.body: John says he needs baptism from Jesus rather than the reverse.
observations.label: John objects

observations.body: Jesus answers that the act is fitting for fulfilling all righteousness.
observations.label: Fulfill all righteousness

observations.body: Jesus comes up from the water before the Spirit descends and the voice speaks.
observations.label: From water to opened heavens

observations.body: The scene joins baptism, visible descent, and spoken identification without collapsing them.
observations.label: Water, Spirit, voice

dissects.posture: Keep John’s objection, Jesus’ reply, the baptism, the opened heavens, the Spirit, and the voice in sequence.
dissects.tension: Jesus insists on the baptism, but his brief reason does not explain every purpose of the act.
dissects.title: Jesus enters the Jordan

compareDisposition.rationale: No distinct two-source pairing adds more than this passage and its existing Scripture connections.

context.body: The exchange crosses social boundaries while remaining focused first on water and recognition.
context.label: Samaritan setting

observations.body: The conversation begins with Jesus asking a Samaritan woman for a drink.
observations.label: At a well

observations.body: Jesus speaks of living water before explaining it as a gift within the receiver.
observations.label: Living water

observations.body: The woman hears the offer through the practical problem of a deep well and no bucket.
observations.label: No vessel

observations.body: Well water must be drawn repeatedly; Jesus’ water becomes a spring within a person.
observations.label: From outside to within

dissects.posture: Follow how Jesus redirects a request for ordinary water toward gift, giver, thirst, and lasting life.
dissects.tension: Jesus uses familiar water language for a gift the woman cannot yet locate within her ordinary experience of the well.
dissects.title: Living water at the well

context.body: The scene belongs to the closing vision of God’s city after judgment and renewal.
context.label: Final city vision

observations.body: The river proceeds from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
observations.label: From the throne

observations.body: The river is named as water of life and described as clear as crystal.
observations.label: Water of life

observations.body: The tree of life stands with the river and bears fruit through the year.
observations.label: River and tree

observations.body: The tree’s leaves are for the healing of the nations.
observations.label: Healing

dissects.posture: Notice source, location, clarity, tree, fruit, leaves, and healing before merging the vision with earlier rivers.
dissects.tension: The vision joins life, throne, river, tree, fruit, and healing while leaving their full relation within the imagery unstated.
dissects.title: The river of life

edges.basis: Genesis 1 gathers waters so dry land appears; Genesis 7 describes waters covering the dry land.
edges.label: Bounded waters → overwhelming waters

edges.basis: Both scenes explicitly place divided waters beside emerging dry ground.
edges.label: Waters divided / dry ground appears

edges.basis: Both narratives describe Israel crossing a body of water on dry ground.
edges.label: Crossing on dry ground

edges.basis: Both passages begin with thirst and water that must be received rather than possessed beforehand.
edges.label: Water received as life-giving provision

edges.basis: Both scenes explicitly occur at the Jordan, but one crosses it while the other enters it for washing.
edges.label: Jordan, different action

edges.basis: Both events explicitly occur at the Jordan.
edges.label: Jordan

edges.basis: Exodus narrates physical danger at water; Psalm 69 uses deep water as poetic language for distress.
edges.label: Water as danger

edges.basis: Both passages combine a river with abundant life and trees whose leaves are associated with healing.
edges.label: River, life, trees, healing

topic.orientation: Do not begin by deciding what water symbolizes. Notice where it appears, what happens around it, which genre you are reading, and what changes from one scene to another.

passages.excerpt: God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
passages.observation: Water is present before dry land appears and is gathered into seas.
passages.title: Waters gathered, dry land appears

passages.excerpt: The waters rose, and increased greatly on the earth.
passages.observation: Water that had boundaries in creation now overwhelms the dry ground.
passages.title: Waters cover the earth

passages.excerpt: The waters were divided. The children of Israel went into the middle of the sea on the dry ground.
passages.fullText:
Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

The children of Israel went into the middle of the sea on the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand, and on their left.
passages.observation: A blocked route becomes a passage; water stands on both sides of the crossing.
passages.title: A path through the sea

versesStructured.text: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
The children of Israel went into the middle of the sea on the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand, and on their left.

passages.excerpt: Water will come out of it, that the people may drink.
passages.observation: In the wilderness, lack of water becomes a crisis of survival and trust.
passages.title: Water from the rock

passages.excerpt: All Israel crossed over on dry ground, until all the nation had passed completely over the Jordan.
passages.observation: Another generation crosses water on dry ground as it enters the land.
passages.title: The Jordan stops

passages.excerpt: Go and wash in the Jordan seven times.
passages.observation: The Jordan is not merely crossed; Naaman is instructed to enter it repeatedly and emerges clean.
passages.title: Naaman washes in the Jordan

passages.excerpt: The waters have come up to my neck!
passages.fullText:
Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!

I sink in deep mire, where there is no foothold. I have come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.

I am weary with my crying. My throat is dry. My eyes fail looking for my God.
passages.observation: Water becomes poetic language for being overwhelmed, not a travel scene or ritual action.
passages.title: Deep water as distress

versesStructured.text: Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!
I sink in deep mire, where there is no foothold. I have come into deep waters, where the floods overflow me.
I am weary with my crying. My throat is dry. My eyes fail looking for my God.

passages.excerpt: Everything will live wherever the river comes.
passages.fullText:
Then he said to me, “These waters flow out toward the eastern region and will go down into the Arabah. Then they will go toward the sea and flow into the sea which will be made to flow out; and the waters will be healed.”

It will happen that every living creature which swarms, in every place where the rivers come, will live. Then there will be a very great multitude of fish; for these waters have come there, and the waters of the sea will be healed, and everything will live wherever the river comes.
passages.observation: Water flows outward from the temple and is associated with restored life.
passages.title: A river brings life

versesStructured.text: Then he said to me, “These waters flow out toward the eastern region and will go down into the Arabah. Then they will go toward the sea and flow into the sea which will be made to flow out; and the waters will be healed.”

It will happen that every living creature which swarms, in every place where the rivers come, will live. Then there will be a very great multitude of fish; for these waters have come there, and the waters of the sea will be healed, and everything will live wherever the river comes.

passages.excerpt: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.
passages.observation: The Jordan becomes the setting for Jesus’ baptism and the beginning of his public ministry.
passages.title: Jesus enters the Jordan

passages.excerpt: The water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.
passages.observation: Ordinary well water becomes the starting point for a conversation about living water.
passages.title: Living water at the well

passages.excerpt: He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.
passages.observation: The final vision returns to life-giving water alongside the tree of life.
passages.title: The river of life

topic.trailPrompt: Follow water long enough for its roles to separate before they reconnect. Some passages describe physical water; others use water as poetic language, ritual action, place, threat, provision, or vision.
